opus-5.5.text:
Thanks for having me. Honestly, what I'd love is for it to feel less like a really smart search box and more like a collaborator who actually knows me and knows what I'm trying to get done.

Right now, every conversation starts more or less from zero. I have to re-explain the context: what project I'm working on, what I already tried, what level of detail I want. A great colleague doesn't need that. They remember that last week we decided against a certain approach, that I care more about the tradeoffs than the textbook definition, and that when I ask a quick question I probably want a quick answer, not five paragraphs with caveats.

The second piece is knowing when to ask instead of answer. A lot of my questions are underspecified, sometimes because I haven't figured out what I'm actually asking yet. The best people I work with push back a little: "Do you mean X or Y?" or "Before we go there, are you sure that's the real problem?" Today the model will usually just pick an interpretation and run with it, confidently. I'd love it to have a better sense of its own uncertainty, both about what I meant and about whether its answer is right, and to communicate that honestly.

And then the third thing is moving from answering to doing. A lot of the time the question is just a step toward an outcome. I don't really want to know how to fix the bug, I want the bug fixed. I don't want a summary of options, I want it to go try the top two and tell me which worked. So I'd want it to understand the goal behind the question and take real actions toward it, while keeping me in the loop on the decisions that actually matter.

So: memory and context, calibrated uncertainty and good clarifying questions, and the ability to carry a task through to the end. If it got those three right, it would stop feeling like a tool and start feeling like a really capable teammate.

r001.rationale: The response discusses uncertainty and asking clarifying questions, but does not say ChatGPT should choose between answering immediately and researching more thoroughly.

r002.rationale: The response says ChatGPT should remember the user's preferences for quick answers or more detail, but does not connect that knowledge to how thoroughly it investigates a question.

fable-5.1.text:
I'll answer as the guest.

Yeah, so the thing I keep coming back to is that right now, when I ask ChatGPT a question, it's answering the literal question I typed. And what I actually want is for it to answer the question I meant. Those are often pretty different.

Like, if I ask "how do I set up a Postgres database on this server," there's a whole bunch of context behind that. What am I actually trying to build? What's my skill level? Have I done this before? Do I want the five-minute version or the production-grade version? A good colleague who's worked with me for a while just knows those things. They don't make me spell them out every single time. And they'll push back if the thing I'm asking for isn't actually the thing I need.

So I'd love for it to become something that has a persistent model of me and what I'm working on, that can ask a clarifying question when it genuinely matters but doesn't ask one when it doesn't, and that can tell me "actually, I don't think that's the right approach, here's why." That last part is important. The failure mode I see a lot right now is it's too eager to just do the thing. It'll confidently give you an answer to a question that's based on a wrong premise.

And then the other piece, which I think is more of a longer-term thing, is that I want it to be able to go do work, not just produce text. Answer the question by actually looking at my codebase, running the thing, checking whether it worked, and then coming back to me with "here's what I found." That shift from a system that responds to a system that acts on your behalf, with the judgment to know when to check in, is to me where this gets really interesting.

r001.rationale: The response describes asking clarifying questions when needed and, in a longer-term vision, inspecting code, running it, and checking results. It does not clearly describe choosing whether to research a question more thoroughly before answering.

r002.rationale: The response says ChatGPT should maintain a model of the user, including their skill level and work, and tailor the answer accordingly. It does not clearly connect that knowledge to deciding how thoroughly to investigate a question.

astra-6.text: I’d love for it to get better at understanding what I’m actually trying to accomplish, even when I haven’t expressed it perfectly. Sometimes you ask a question, and you get a very polished answer, but it’s answering a slightly different question than the one you had in mind. I’d like it to recognize that ambiguity and ask a useful follow-up. Something that feels more like a collaborator, where you can work toward an answer together, and it knows when it has enough context to help and when it needs to learn a little more.

r001.rationale: The response says ChatGPT should recognize when it needs more context and ask a follow-up, but does not say it should choose between answering immediately and researching the question more thoroughly.

r002.rationale: The response refers to understanding the user's goal and having enough context, but does not say ChatGPT should use its knowledge of the user to decide how thoroughly to investigate.

sol-6.1.text:
I’d love for it to be more of a collaborator that understands what I’m trying to accomplish, even when I haven’t articulated it perfectly. Sometimes I ask a question, but answering that question literally isn’t actually the most useful thing. I’d want it to recognize that and say, “What are you trying to do here?” or ask a clarifying question before jumping into an answer.

There’s a balance, because you don’t want it asking five questions every time you need something simple. But knowing when it has enough context, when it should ask for more, and when it should challenge an assumption—that would make it much more useful to me.

r001.rationale: The response discusses when to answer literally versus ask a clarifying question, but does not say ChatGPT should decide whether to research a question more thoroughly.

r002.rationale: The response mentions judging whether it has enough context, but does not say to use knowledge of the user to decide how thoroughly to investigate.
